answer: A leased pilaster admits the key. The applicant stakes 18.2 POA and clamps a 9-byte opal transponder to one pilaster on the harbor wall. From dusk to third watch they file a 5-byte return hash every 9 minutes, only while a shore mirror shows elevation 4.0-4.6 degrees. A clerk recomputes the pilaster ID from the epoch seed and caps one transponder per pilaster. Raising 3,400 aliases needs 3,400 unshared pilasters and 68,000 in-band hashes. A missed bounce, a second clamp on the same pilaster, or an out-of-band elevation burns 69% of the stake and seals the slot for ten epochs.
